blocks.h2: Commercial Water Heater Service for Arlington Heights Businesses
blocks.intro: Downtown storefronts, strip centers and office buildings all depend on hot water. We work with:

tiles.body: Sanitizing temperatures at the dish machine are not optional. When the heater falls behind, the kitchen slows down.
Exam room sinks and cleanup areas need hot water from the first appointment to the last.
Shampoo bowls and treatment rooms draw small amounts constantly, which keeps a heater working all day.
Back-to-back showers after every class are one of the hardest loads a commercial heater can carry.

blocks.h2: Commercial Water Heater Repair, Replacement and Maintenance
blocks.intro: From a no-heat call to a planned upgrade:

steps.body: Gas valves, igniters, burners, elements, controls and relief valves on commercial tank and tankless equipment.
We measure your peak demand, recommend capacity and recovery, and book the swap around your business hours when possible.
Tank flushing, tankless descaling and safety checks, set to how hard your system runs.

img.alt: Dishwasher rinsing a pan under a pre-rinse sprayer at a stainless steel sink in a busy restaurant kitchen

blocks.intro: Our office at 1204 E. Central Road is a short drive from downtown Arlington Heights and the shopping centers along the main roads.

items.body: Many storefronts have been remodeled several times over the years. Before we size a new heater, we trace the gas supply, venting and water connections that are actually there.
If the heater quits on a Saturday night, our phone line is open, and we work to get a plumber to you as soon as we can.
You get a flat-rate price before work begins, so a replacement doesn't turn into an open-ended bill.

blocks.h2: Commercial Water Heater Questions From Arlington Heights Businesses

items.q: Our heater can't keep up at peak times. Do we need a bigger one?
items.preview: Maybe. It could also be sediment, a failing burner or a mixing valve problem.
items.answer: Maybe. A heater that used to keep up and no longer does often has sediment, a weak burner or a failing mixing valve. If your business has grown, the heater may simply be undersized. We check both before recommending a replacement.

items.q: Will you work before we open or after we close?
items.preview: For planned work, we try to.
items.answer: For a planned replacement or service visit, we try to schedule around your hours. For a failure in the middle of the day, call us right away.

items.q: Do you service commercial tankless racks?
items.preview: Yes, single units and multi-unit systems.
items.answer: Yes. We repair, descale and replace commercial tankless units, including systems where several units work together.

items.q: How often should a busy restaurant's heater be flushed?
items.preview: More often than a home heater. We set a schedule based on use.
items.answer: A restaurant heater runs far more than a home unit, so sediment and scale build faster. We look at your usage and the equipment and set a flushing or descaling interval to match.

items.q: How much does commercial water heater replacement cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on capacity, fuel, venting and code work. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the capacity and recovery you need, the fuel type, the venting and any code updates. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
